nfl.oneThing: Jeffery Simmons is headed to the Chicago Bears from Tennessee, the biggest move so far ahead of the November 10 trade deadline.

headlines.title: Bears land Jeffery Simmons ahead of the deadline
headlines.summary: Chicago have acquired defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons and a 2028 fifth-round pick from Tennessee. The Bears gave up a 2027 first-round pick, a 2027 fourth-round pick and a 2028 first-round pick to get him. ESPN's deadline tracker also has Colts guard Quenton Nelson on the move. The deadline is November 10, but deals have already started. Chicago are 5-2 and host Seattle on Monday night.
headlines.whyItMatters: Simmons adds interior pressure to a Bears team that sits fifth in the NFC.

headlines.title: Cowboys beat the Eagles 38–21 and now host the Cardinals
headlines.summary: Dallas (3-4) won 38–21 on the road against Philadelphia, a division win. Javonte Williams ran for a career-high 155 yards of the team's 204. The Cowboys had the second-worst rushing offence in the NFL before the game. Their defence needed three quarters to settle down against a Philadelphia offence hit hard by injuries. Next up is Arizona (2-5) on Sunday, the first of four home games in five weeks.
headlines.whyItMatters: Dallas need to show they can be consistent, having won only one streak under coach Brian Schottenheimer.

headlines.title: Jaguars host the Colts as Indianapolis rebuild
headlines.summary: Jacksonville (4-2) host Indianapolis (2-5), who have lost three in a row and 12 of their last 14 dating back to last season. The Jaguars have won 11 straight home games against the Colts, a streak left tackle Walker Little called weird and quirky. Indianapolis traded captain DeForest Buckner and guard Quenton Nelson this week to start a rebuild. Coach Shane Steichen says the team has a job to do regardless.
headlines.whyItMatters: A win would keep Jacksonville among the AFC's top four seeds.

teamNews.title: Raiders injury report ahead of the Jets
teamNews.text: Patrick Johnson missed Wednesday's practice with a neck stinger, and Ian Thomas was limited with a shoulder injury.

teamNews.title: Four-game slide
teamNews.text: The Raiders (3-4) have lost four straight after a 3-0 start. In the 35–21 loss to the Rams, they ran for 48 yards to the Rams' 199. Klint Kubiak said the team won't run the ball until it stops the run.

teamNews.title: Laulu released; Thornton back from IR
teamNews.text: The Raiders released defensive tackle Jonah Laulu this week, and the Titans claimed him on waivers. He played 23% of defensive snaps this year, down from 68% in 2025. Dont'e Thornton was activated off injured reserve, but he has no set role and has to beat somebody out.

headlines.title: Anthony Edwards has knee surgery
headlines.summary: Timberwolves star Anthony Edwards had a debridement on his right knee at the Mayo Clinic on Thursday, the team announced. The procedure removes damaged cartilage, bone spurs or loose fragments to relieve pain and improve movement, according to the Mayo Clinic. The team expects a full recovery but has not given a timeline. ESPN's Shams Charania reports Edwards could be out for up to two months. He has dealt with right knee pain since last spring and played a career-low 61 games last season. Edwards is second in the league in scoring at 33.2 points a game.
headlines.whyItMatters: Minnesota are 3-2 and eighth in the West, so a long absence for Edwards would reshape their season.

headlines.title: Jaylen Brown denies demanding a Celtics trade
headlines.summary: Jaylen Brown, now with the 76ers, has pushed back on what he called false allegations from Brian Scalabrine. He denied giving Boston a list of ultimatums or a trade demand this summer. Brown says he is ready to move on. He had 20 points and 10 rebounds in Philadelphia's 114–109 win at Indiana.
headlines.whyItMatters: Philadelphia are 4-1 and second in the East, and Brown is a central part of that start.

headlines.title: Kyrie Irving draws strong trade interest
headlines.summary: Sources told ESPN that Kyrie Irving would command a robust trade market if Dallas made him available. For now, Irving and president Masai Ujiri have both signalled a shared commitment to building alongside Cooper Flagg. Ujiri said the front office believes Irving can thrive in the new setup. Flagg had 26 points, 8 assists and 5 rebounds in Dallas's 120–96 win over Oklahoma City, and Irving scored 15.
headlines.whyItMatters: Dallas are 3-2 and seventh in the West, and Irving's future is a big question for the front office.

headlines.title: Miami finally win, beating the Hawks 129–117
headlines.summary: Miami had lost their first four games, but Giannis Antetokounmpo had 24 points and 18 rebounds in a 129–117 win at Atlanta. Bam Adebayo added 24 points, nine rebounds and three steals. Kingston Flemings and Nickeil Alexander-Walker each scored 23 for the Hawks, who lost after going 2-2.
headlines.whyItMatters: The win moves the Heat to 1-4 and ends their 0-4 start, but they are still 13th in the East.

contextCard.title: How the NBA Cup works
contextCard.body: The NBA Cup is an in-season tournament. Teams are split into groups, and the top teams from each group advance to a knockout stage that ends in a championship game. Group games are played alongside the regular season, so the tournament runs through the early months of the year.
